correctness.rationale: The Laplacian of K_k vee H has n as the nonconstant clique/contrast eigenvalue and restricts to kI+L_H on residual zero-sum vectors. Exact projector arithmetic yields the three block identities. Convexity makes the residual rank-one correction nonnegative, and the shifted nonnegative matrix B=Delta I-L_H gives F_p(h(kI+L_H))=sum h^j F_{p-j}(s)B^j/j!, whose coefficients are nonnegative for s <=1. F_p(nh)<=1 exactly up to beta_p, and every clique-to-residual entry becomes strictly negative afterward. All stated boundaries and quantifiers are proved. Exact fraction verifier passed 222 graph/order cases and 231840 entry comparisons; tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The generic nonnegative-coefficient shift applied directly to the whole join Laplacian uses its maximum degree n-1 and gives at most h <=1/(n-1) by the first-order Taylor remainder coefficient; it does not establish the larger exact beta_p/n threshold. The current proof isolates the dominating clique eigenvalue and shifts only the residual block, which is an additional implication not supplied by the broad criteria.

value.rationale: The result gives one exact sharp step-size constant for all even Taylor orders and infinitely many nonsymmetric and disconnected residual cores, with no matrix entry root searches. It explains an improvement over the generic full-matrix coefficient positivity estimate by isolating the dominating-clique rank-one obstruction, produces a strict core-block positivity guarantee, and yields exact thresholds for long fan and wheel graph families. The natural object is positivity-preserving graph heat diffusion on networks with dominant hubs, and the specific beta_p/n threshold is simultaneously necessary and sufficient in the stated sparse-core regime.
